sanskrit: ete cānye ca bahavo brāhmaṇāḥ saṃśitavratāḥ sadasyā abhavaṃs tatra satre pārikṣitasya ha
english: These and many other Brāhmaṇas of keen vows were the assembly-members at the snake-sacrifice of the son of Parīkṣit.

sanskrit: juhvatsv ṛtvikṣv atha tadā sarpasatre mahākratau ahayaḥ prāpataṃs tatra ghorāḥ prāṇibhayāvahāḥ
english: As the priests were offering oblations at that great rite, the snake-sacrifice, terrible serpents fell there, striking terror into all living creatures.

sanskrit: vasāmedovahāḥ kulyā nāgānāṃ saṃpravartitāḥ vavau gandhaś ca tumulo dahyatām aniśaṃ tadā
english: Streams of fat and marrow flowed from the serpents; and continuously, day and night, a tumultuous smell of burning rose from those that were being consumed.

sanskrit: patatāṃ caiva nāgānāṃ dhiṣṭhitānāṃ tathāmbare aśrūyatāniśaṃ śabdaḥ pacyatāṃ cāgninā bhṛśam
english: The sound of those serpents falling and of those hovering in the sky was heard incessantly, as they were consumed with great intensity by the fire.

sanskrit: takṣakas tu sa nāgendraḥ puraṃdaraniveśanam gataḥ śrutvaiva rājānaṃ dīkṣitaṃ janamejayam
english: But Takṣaka, that lord of serpents, hearing that king Janamejaya had been consecrated, fled to the abode of Indra, the Destroyer of Pura.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarvaṃ yathāvṛttam ākhyāya bhujagottamaḥ agacchac charaṇaṃ bhīta āgaskṛtvā puraṃdaram
english: Then, having told everything that had come to pass, that best of serpents, terror-stricken and conscious of his offence, sought refuge with Indra, the Destroyer of Pura.

sanskrit: tam indraḥ prāha suprīto na tavāstīha takṣaka bhayaṃ nāgendra tasmād vai sarpasatrāt kathaṃ cana
english: Indra, greatly pleased, said to him: "O Takṣaka, O lord of serpents, you have nothing to fear here from that snake-sacrifice under any circumstances."

sanskrit: prasādito mayā pūrvaṃ tavārthāya pitāmahaḥ tasmāt tava bhayaṃ nāsti vyetu te mānaso jvaraḥ
english: "The Grandsire was formerly propitiated by me on your behalf; therefore you have nothing to fear — let the fever of your mind depart."

sanskrit: evam āśvāsitas tena tataḥ sa bhujagottamaḥ uvāsa bhavane tatra śakrasya muditaḥ sukhī
english: Thus reassured by him, that best of serpents then dwelt in Śakra's mansion, joyful and at ease.

sanskrit: ajasraṃ nipatatsv agnau nāgeṣu bhṛśaduḥkhitaḥ alpaśeṣaparīvāro vāsukiḥ paryatapyata
english: As serpents fell ceaselessly into the fire, Vāsuki, with his retinue much reduced, was greatly distressed and burned with anguish.

sanskrit: kaśmalaṃ cāviśad ghoraṃ vāsukiṃ pannageśvaram sa ghūrṇamānahṛdayo bhaginīm idam abravīt
english: A terrible stupor seized Vāsuki, lord of serpents; his heart reeling, he spoke thus to his sister:

sanskrit: dahyante 'ṅgāni me bhadre diśo na pratibhānti ca sīdāmīva ca saṃmohād ghūrṇatīva ca me manaḥ
english: "My limbs burn, dear sister; the directions are unclear to me; I am as if sinking in confusion, and my mind seems to whirl."

sanskrit: dṛṣṭir bhramati me 'tīva hṛdayaṃ dīryatīva ca patiṣyāmy avaśo 'dyāhaṃ tasmin dīpte vibhāvasau
english: "My vision spins exceedingly, and my heart seems to burst; today I shall fall helplessly into that blazing fire."

sanskrit: pārikṣitasya yajño 'sau vartate 'smajjighāṃsayā vyaktaṃ mayāpi gantavyaṃ pitṛrājaniveśanam
english: "That sacrifice of Parīkṣit's son is proceeding with intent to destroy us; clearly I too must go to the abode of the king of the dead."

sanskrit: ayaṃ sa kālaḥ saṃprāpto yadartham asi me svasaḥ jaratkāroḥ purā dattā sā trāhy asmān sabāndhavān
english: "This is the moment for which you, my sister, were given in marriage to Jaratkāru long ago — protect us now together with all our kindred."

sanskrit: āstīkaḥ kila yajñaṃ taṃ vartantaṃ bhujagottame pratiṣetsyati māṃ pūrvaṃ svayam āha pitāmahaḥ
english: "The Grandsire himself previously told me that Āstīka would indeed stop that sacrifice when it was proceeding with the best of serpents as its victim."

sanskrit: tad vatse brūhi vatsaṃ svaṃ kumāraṃ vṛddhasaṃmatam mamādya tvaṃ sabhṛtyasya mokṣārthaṃ vedavittamam
english: "Therefore, dear child, speak today to your own son, that youth revered by the elders, that foremost knower of the Vedas, for the liberation of me and my servants."

sanskrit: sūta uvāca tata āhūya putraṃ svaṃ jaratkārur bhujaṃgamā vāsuker nāgarājasya vacanād idam abravīt
english: The Sūta said: Then Jaratkāru, the female serpent, summoning her own son, spoke these words at the bidding of Vāsuki, king of serpents:

sanskrit: ahaṃ tava pituḥ putra bhrātrā dattā nimittataḥ kālaḥ sa cāyaṃ saṃprāptas tat kuruṣva yathātatham
english: "I was given to your father, my son, by my brother for a purpose; that moment has now arrived — do what is required of you accordingly."

sanskrit: āstīka uvāca kiṃnimittaṃ mama pitur dattā tvaṃ mātulena me tan mamācakṣva tattvena śrutvā kartāsmi tat tathā
english: Āstīka said: "For what purpose were you given to my father by my maternal uncle? Tell me the truth of it — having heard, I shall act accordingly."

sanskrit: sūta uvāca tata ācaṣṭa sā tasmai bāndhavānāṃ hitaiṣiṇī bhaginī nāgarājasya jaratkārur aviklavā
english: The Sūta said: Then she, the sister of the king of serpents, Jaratkāru, composed and well-wishing toward her kindred, told him this:

sanskrit: bhujagānām aśeṣāṇāṃ mātā kadrūr iti śrutiḥ tayā śaptā ruṣitayā sutā yasmān nibodha tat
english: "The mother of all the serpents without exception is known as Kadrū; by her, angered, were her sons cursed — hear the reason for that."

sanskrit: ucchaiḥśravāḥ so 'śvarājo yan mithyā na kṛto mama vinatānimittaṃ paṇite dāsabhāvāya putrakāḥ
english: "Ucchaihshravas, that king of horses — because you did not make him falsely mine in the wager made for Vinatā's sake, my sons, for the sake of enslaving her."

sanskrit: janamejayasya vo yajñe dhakṣyaty anilasārathiḥ tatra pañcatvam āpannāḥ pretalokaṃ gamiṣyatha
english: "'At Janamejaya's sacrifice, the fire whose charioteer is the wind shall burn you; meeting dissolution there, you shall go to the world of the dead.'"

sanskrit: tāṃ ca śaptavatīm evaṃ sākṣāl lokapitāmahaḥ evam astv iti tad vākyaṃ provācānumumoda ca
english: "And the Grandsire of the world himself, seeing her who had thus cursed, spoke the words 'So be it' and approved of it."

sanskrit: vāsukiś cāpi tac chrutvā pitāmahavacas tadā amṛte mathite tāta devāñ śaraṇam īyivān
english: "And Vāsuki, hearing that word of the Grandsire at the time the nectar was being churned, O dear one, sought the refuge of the gods."

sanskrit: siddhārthāś ca surāḥ sarve prāpyāmṛtam anuttamam bhrātaraṃ me puraskṛtya prajāpatim upāgaman
english: "And all the gods, having attained the peerless nectar and their purpose fulfilled, with my brother at their head, approached Prajāpati."

sanskrit: te taṃ prasādayām āsur devāḥ sarve pitāmaham rājñā vāsukinā sārdhaṃ sa śāpo na bhaved iti
english: "All the gods together propitiated the Grandsire along with king Vāsuki, that the curse might not take effect."

sanskrit: vāsukir nāgarājo 'yaṃ duḥkhito jñātikāraṇāt abhiśāpaḥ sa mātrāsya bhagavan na bhaved iti
english: "'This Vāsuki, king of serpents, is distressed on account of his kinsmen; let not this curse from his mother come to pass, O Lord.'"

sanskrit: brahmovāca jaratkārur jaratkāruṃ yāṃ bhāryāṃ samavāpsyati tatra jāto dvijaḥ śāpād bhujagān mokṣayiṣyati
english: "Brahmā said: 'A twice-born one born to Jaratkāru from the wife named Jaratkāru whom he shall obtain will deliver the serpents from the curse.'"

sanskrit: jaratkārur uvāca etac chrutvā tu vacanaṃ vāsukiḥ pannageśvaraḥ prādān mām amaraprakhya tava pitre mahātmane prāg evānāgate kāle tatra tvaṃ mayy ajāyathāḥ
english: Jaratkāru said: "Hearing this speech, Vāsuki, lord of serpents, gave me, O one equal to the immortals, to your father, the great-souled one, even before the time came; therein you were born of me."

sanskrit: ayaṃ sa kālaḥ saṃprāpto bhayān nas trātum arhasi bhrātaraṃ caiva me tasmāt trātum arhasi pāvakāt
english: "This is that moment now arrived — you must rescue us from fear; you must rescue my brother as well from the fire."

sanskrit: amoghaṃ naḥ kṛtaṃ tat syād yad ahaṃ tava dhīmate pitre dattā vimokṣārthaṃ kathaṃ vā putra manyase
english: "That act of mine would not be in vain — that I was given to your wise father for the sake of liberation. What do you think, my son?"

sanskrit: sūta uvāca evam uktas tathety uktvā so 'stīko mātaraṃ tadā abravīd duḥkhasaṃtaptaṃ vāsukiṃ jīvayann iva
english: The Sūta said: Thus addressed, having said "So be it," Āstīka then spoke to his mother and, as if reviving Vāsuki, who was burning with sorrow:

sanskrit: ahaṃ tvāṃ mokṣayiṣyāmi vāsuke pannagottama tasmāc chāpān mahāsattva satyam etad bravīmi te
english: "I will rescue you, O Vāsuki, O best of serpents, from that curse, O great being — this I tell you truly."

sanskrit: bhava svasthamanā nāga na hi te vidyate bhayam prayatiṣye tathā saumya yathā śreyo bhaviṣyati na me vāg anṛtaṃ prāha svaireṣv api kuto 'nyathā
english: "Be of easy mind, O serpent — there is no fear for you. I shall strive in such a way that what is beneficial will come about. My speech has never spoken untruth even in play — how then otherwise?"

sanskrit: taṃ vai nṛpavaraṃ gatvā dīkṣitaṃ janamejayam vāgbhir maṅgalayuktābhis toṣayiṣye 'dya mātula yathā sa yajño nṛpater nirvartiṣyati sattama
english: "Going to that best of kings, the consecrated Janamejaya, I shall today please him with words full of auspicious praise, O maternal uncle, in such a way that the king's sacrifice will be brought to a close, O noble one."

sanskrit: sa saṃbhāvaya nāgendra mayi sarvaṃ mahāmate na te mayi mano jātu mithyā bhavitum arhati
english: "O lord of serpents, O great-minded one, place all trust in me — your mind ought never to prove false in regard to me."

sanskrit: vāsukir uvāca āstīka parighūrṇāmi hṛdayaṃ me vidīryate diśaś ca na prajānāmi brahmadaṇḍanipīḍitaḥ
english: Vāsuki said: "Āstīka, I reel all around; my heart is bursting; I do not recognise the directions, crushed as I am by the rod of Brahmā's curse."

sanskrit: āstīka uvāca na saṃtāpas tvayā kāryaḥ kathaṃ cit pannagottama dīptād agneḥ samutpannaṃ nāśayiṣyāmi te bhayam
english: Āstīka said: "You must not grieve in any way, O best of serpents — I will destroy your fear that has arisen from the blazing fire."

sanskrit: brahmadaṇḍaṃ mahāghoraṃ kālāgnisamatejasam nāśayiṣyāmi mātra tvaṃ bhayaṃ kārṣīḥ kathaṃ cana
english: "I will destroy the great and terrible rod of Brahmā's curse, equal in energy to the fire of dissolution — mother, you must not fear in any way."

sanskrit: sūta uvāca tataḥ sa vāsuker ghoram apanīya manojvaram ādhāya cātmano 'ṅgeṣu jagāma tvarito bhṛśam
english: The Sūta said: Then, having removed the terrible anguish of mind from Vāsuki and bearing it upon his own limbs, he set forth with great haste.

sanskrit: janamejayasya taṃ yajñaṃ sarvaiḥ samuditaṃ guṇaiḥ mokṣāya bhujagendrāṇām āstīko dvijasattamaḥ
english: That foremost of twice-born men, Āstīka, went to Janamejaya's sacrifice, endowed with all its qualities, for the liberation of the lords of serpents.

sanskrit: sa gatvāpaśyad āstīko yajñāyatanam uttamam vṛtaṃ sadasyair bahubhiḥ sūryavahnisamaprabhaiḥ
english: Going there, Āstīka beheld that excellent sacrificial ground surrounded by many assembly-members of a brilliance equal to the sun and fire.

sanskrit: sa tatra vārito dvāḥsthaiḥ praviśan dvijasattamaḥ abhituṣṭāva taṃ yajñaṃ praveśārthī dvijottamaḥ
english: Stopped there at the gate by the doorkeepers as he sought to enter, that best of twice-born men, that foremost among the twice-born, praised the sacrifice in order to gain admittance.

sanskrit: āstīka uvāca somasya yajño varuṇasya yajñaḥ; prajāpater yajña āsīt prayāge tathā yajño 'yaṃ tava bhāratāgrya; pārikṣita svasti no 'stu priyebhyaḥ
english: Āstīka said: "The sacrifice of Soma, the sacrifice of Varuṇa, the sacrifice of Prajāpati performed at Prayāga — such is this sacrifice of yours, O foremost of the Bharatas, O son of Parīkṣit. May there be welfare to us and to our dear ones!"

sanskrit: śakrasya yajñaḥ śatasaṃkhya uktas; tathāparas tulyasaṃkhyaḥ śataṃ vai tathā yajño 'yaṃ tava bhāratāgrya; pārikṣita svasti no 'stu priyebhyaḥ
english: "The sacrifice of Śakra is said to be one hundred in number; another equally counted is verily a hundred — such is this sacrifice of yours, O foremost of the Bharatas, O son of Parīkṣit. May there be welfare to us and to our dear ones!"

sanskrit: yamasya yajño harimedhasaś ca; yathā yajño rantidevasya rājñaḥ tathā yajño 'yaṃ tava bhāratāgrya; pārikṣita svasti no 'stu priyebhyaḥ
english: "As was the sacrifice of Yama and of Harishmedha, as was the sacrifice of king Rantideva — such is this sacrifice of yours, O foremost of the Bharatas, O son of Parīkṣit. May there be welfare to us and to our dear ones!"

sanskrit: gayasya yajñaḥ śaśabindoś ca rājño; yajñas tathā vaiśravaṇasya rājñaḥ tathā yajño 'yaṃ tava bhāratāgrya; pārikṣita svasti no 'stu priyebhyaḥ
english: "The sacrifice of Gaya, the sacrifice of king Śaśabindu, and the sacrifice of king Vaiśravaṇa — such is this sacrifice of yours, O foremost of the Bharatas, O son of Parīkṣit. May there be welfare to us and to our dear ones!"

sanskrit: nṛgasya yajñas tv ajamīḍhasya cāsīd; yathā yajño dāśaratheś ca rājñaḥ tathā yajño 'yaṃ tava bhāratāgrya; pārikṣita svasti no 'stu priyebhyaḥ
english: "The sacrifice of Nṛga and that of Ajamidha, as was the sacrifice of king Dāśarathi — such is this sacrifice of yours, O foremost of the Bharatas, O son of Parīkṣit. May there be welfare to us and to our dear ones!"

sanskrit: yajñaḥ śruto no divi devasūnor; yudhiṣṭhirasyājamīḍhasya rājñaḥ tathā yajño 'yaṃ tava bhāratāgrya; pārikṣita svasti no 'stu priyebhyaḥ
english: "We have heard of the sacrifice in heaven of the son of the gods, the sacrifice of king Yudhiṣṭhira, the descendant of Ajamidha — such is this sacrifice of yours, O foremost of the Bharatas, O son of Parīkṣit. May there be welfare to us and to our dear ones!"

sanskrit: kṛṣṇasya yajñaḥ satyavatyāḥ sutasya; svayaṃ ca karma pracakāra yatra tathā yajño 'yaṃ tava bhāratāgrya; pārikṣita svasti no 'stu priyebhyaḥ
english: "The sacrifice of Kṛṣṇa, the son of Satyavatī, wherein he himself performed the rites — such is this sacrifice of yours, O foremost of the Bharatas, O son of Parīkṣit. May there be welfare to us and to our dear ones!"

sanskrit: ime hi te sūryahutāśavarcasaḥ; samāsate vṛtrahaṇaḥ kratuṃ yathā naiṣāṃ jñānaṃ vidyate jñātum adya; dattaṃ yebhyo na praṇaśyet kathaṃ cit
english: "For these ones here of a brilliance like the sun and fire are seated as at the rite of the Slayer of Vṛtra; no knowledge exists today to fully comprehend them — what is given to them can never in any way be lost."

sanskrit: ṛtviksamo nāsti lokeṣu caiva; dvaipāyaneneti viniścitaṃ me etasya śiṣyā hi kṣitiṃ caranti; sarvartvijaḥ karmasu sveṣu dakṣāḥ
english: "There is no equal to Dvaipāyana as a priest anywhere in the worlds — this is my firm conviction. For his disciples walk this earth as officiant priests, all skilled in their respective rites."

sanskrit: vibhāvasuś citrabhānur mahātmā; hiraṇyaretā viśvabhuk kṛṣṇavartmā pradakṣiṇāvartaśikhaḥ pradīpto; havyaṃ tavedaṃ hutabhug vaṣṭi devaḥ
english: "Vibhāvasu, Citrabhānu, the great-souled one, bearer of golden seed, all-consumer, dark-pathed, with flame spiralling rightward, blazing — the god who is the eater of oblations desires this offering of yours."

sanskrit: neha tvad anyo vidyate jīvaloke; samo nṛpaḥ pālayitā prajānām dhṛtyā ca te prītamanāḥ sadāhaṃ; tvaṃ vā rājā dharmarājo yamo vā
english: "There is no other king found in this world of the living equal to you as a protector of subjects; I am always glad at heart by your steadfastness — you are either the king Dharmarāja or Yama himself."

sanskrit: śakraḥ sākṣād vajrapāṇir yatheha; trātā loke 'smiṃs tvaṃ tatheha prajānām matas tvaṃ naḥ puruṣendreha loke; na ca tvad anyo gṛhapatir asti yajñe
english: "As Śakra, the thunderbolt-wielding Indra himself, is protector in this world, so are you here the protector of subjects; you are esteemed by us as the lord of men in this world — and there is none other than you who is master of this sacrifice."

sanskrit: khaṭvāṅganābhāgadilīpakalpo; yayātimāndhātṛsamaprabhāvaḥ ādityatejaḥpratimānatejā; bhīṣmo yathā bhrājasi suvratas tvam
english: "Equal to Khatvanga, Nābhāga, and Dilīpa, of prowess comparable to Yayāti and Māndhātā, of energy matching the brilliance of the Ādityas — you shine, O Suvarata, like Bhīṣma."

sanskrit: vālmīkivat te nibhṛtaṃ sudhairyaṃ; vasiṣṭhavat te niyataś ca kopaḥ prabhutvam indreṇa samaṃ mataṃ me; dyutiś ca nārāyaṇavad vibhāti
english: "Your composure is as firm as Vālmīki's; your anger is as restrained as Vasiṣṭha's; your lordship I deem equal to that of Indra; and your radiance shines like Nārāyaṇa's."

sanskrit: yamo yathā dharmaviniścayajñaḥ; kṛṣṇo yathā sarvaguṇopapannaḥ śriyāṃ nivāso 'si yathā vasūnāṃ; nidhānabhūto 'si tathā kratūnām
english: "As Yama you know the determination of dharma; as Kṛṣṇa you are endowed with every virtue; as Śrī is the abode of the Vasus, so are you the repository of sacrifices."

sanskrit: dambhodbhavenāsi samo balena; rāmo yathā śastravid astravic ca aurvatritābhyām asi tulyatejā; duṣprekṣaṇīyo 'si bhagīratho vā
english: "In strength you are equal to Dambhodbhava; like Rāma you are versed in weapons and missiles; in energy you are equal to Aurva and Trita; you are hard to look upon as the sun, or like Bhagīratha."

sanskrit: sūta uvāca evaṃ stutāḥ sarva eva prasannā; rājā sadasyā ṛtvijo havyavāhaḥ teṣāṃ dṛṣṭvā bhāvitānīṅgitāni; provāca rājā janamejayo 'tha
english: The Sūta said: Thus praised, all of them — the king, the assembly-members, the priests, and the bearer of oblations — were pleased. Seeing the contented gestures of all of them, king Janamejaya then spoke:

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca bālo vākyaṃ sthavira iva prabhāṣate; nāyaṃ bālaḥ sthaviro 'yaṃ mato me icchāmy ahaṃ varam asmai pradātuṃ; tan me viprā vitaradhvaṃ sametāḥ
english: Janamejaya said: "This boy speaks like an elder; this is no boy — he is an elder in my estimation. I wish to grant him a boon — O Brāhmaṇas, assembled together, permit me this."

sanskrit: sadasyā ūcuḥ bālo 'pi vipro mānya eveha rājñāṃ; yaś cāvidvān yaś ca vidvān yathāvat sarvān kāmāṃs tvatta eṣo 'rhate 'dya; yathā ca nas takṣaka eti śīghram
english: The assembly-members said: "Even a Brahmin boy is always worthy of honour from kings, whether unlearned or learned. He deserves all wishes from you properly today — and let Takṣaka come quickly to us."

sanskrit: sūta uvāca vyāhartukāme varade nṛpe dvijaṃ; varaṃ vṛṇīṣveti tato 'bhyuvāca hotā vākyaṃ nātihṛṣṭāntarātmā; karmaṇy asmiṃs takṣako naiti tāvat
english: The Sūta said: As the boon-granting king was about to speak, offering a boon to the twice-born youth, the Hotā then said with a heart not excessively joyful: "Choose a boon" — for Takṣaka had not yet come to the rite.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca yathā cedaṃ karma samāpyate me; yathā ca nas takṣaka eti śīghram tathā bhavantaḥ prayatantu sarve; paraṃ śaktyā sa hi me vidviṣāṇaḥ
english: Janamejaya said: "May all of you strive with your utmost power that this rite of mine be completed and that Takṣaka comes quickly to us — for he is my enemy."

sanskrit: ṛtvija ūcuḥ yathā śāstrāṇi naḥ prāhur yathā śaṃsati pāvakaḥ indrasya bhavane rājaṃs takṣako bhayapīḍitaḥ
english: The officiating priests said: "As the scriptures tell us, and as the fire itself indicates — O king, Takṣaka is in the mansion of Indra, oppressed by fear."

sanskrit: sūta uvāca yathā sūto lohitākṣo mahātmā; paurāṇiko veditavān purastāt sa rājānaṃ prāha pṛṣṭas tadānīṃ; yathāhur viprās tadvad etan nṛdeva
english: The Sūta said: "Just as the great-souled Sūta Lohitākṣa, the Puranic bard, had known this beforehand and told the king when asked at that time — even as the Brāhmaṇas declare it, so is this the case, O lord of men."

sanskrit: purāṇam āgamya tato bravīmy ahaṃ; dattaṃ tasmai varam indreṇa rājan vaseha tvaṃ matsakāśe sugupto; na pāvakas tvāṃ pradahiṣyatīti
english: "'Drawing on the Purāṇa, I tell you this: Indra gave him that boon, O king: "Dwell here in my presence, well protected — the fire shall not burn you."'"

sanskrit: etac chrutvā dīkṣitas tapyamāna; āste hotāraṃ codayan karmakāle hotā ca yattaḥ sa juhāva mantrair; atho indraḥ svayam evājagāma
english: Hearing this, the consecrated king, burning with ardour, sat urging the Hotā on at the time of the rite; the Hotā, alert, offered with mantras — and thereupon Indra himself came in person.

sanskrit: vimānam āruhya mahānubhāvaḥ; sarvair devaiḥ parisaṃstūyamānaḥ balāhakaiś cāpy anugamyamāno; vidyādharair apsarasāṃ gaṇaiś ca
english: Having mounted his celestial vehicle, the great and glorious one was praised by all the gods, accompanied also by Balāhaka spirits, by the Vidyādharas and by hosts of Apsaras.

sanskrit: tasyottarīye nihitaḥ sa nāgo; bhayodvignaḥ śarma naivābhyagacchat tato rājā mantravido 'bravīt punaḥ; kruddho vākyaṃ takṣakasyāntam icchan
english: That serpent, hidden in Indra's upper garment, could find no safety, agitated by fear; then the king, versed in spells, again spoke words in anger, desiring the end of Takṣaka:

sanskrit: indrasya bhavane viprā yadi nāgaḥ sa takṣakaḥ tam indreṇaiva sahitaṃ pātayadhvaṃ vibhāvasau
english: "O Brāhmaṇas, if that serpent Takṣaka is in the mansion of Indra, then hurl him together with Indra himself into the fire."

sanskrit: ṛtvija ūcuḥ ayam āyāti vai tūrṇaṃ takṣakas te vaśaṃ nṛpa śrūyate 'sya mahān nādo ruvato bhairavaṃ bhayāt
english: The officiating priests said: "Takṣaka is indeed coming quickly under your power, O king; his great cry is heard, roaring terribly out of fear."

sanskrit: nūnaṃ mukto vajrabhṛtā sa nāgo; bhraṣṭaś cāṅkān mantravisrastakāyaḥ ghūrṇann ākāśe naṣṭasaṃjño 'bhyupaiti; tīvrān niḥśvāsān niḥśvasan pannagendraḥ
english: "Surely that serpent has been released by the thunder-bearer; fallen from Indra's embrace, his body loosened by the mantras, that lord of serpents comes whirling through the sky, having lost consciousness, breathing violent breaths."

sanskrit: vartate tava rājendra karmaitad vidhivat prabho asmai tu dvijamukhyāya varaṃ tvaṃ dātum arhasi
english: "This rite of yours is proceeding according to rule, O lord of kings, O master. Now you should grant a boon to this foremost of twice-born men."

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca bālābhirūpasya tavāprameya; varaṃ prayacchāmi yathānurūpam vṛṇīṣva yat te 'bhimataṃ hṛdi sthitaṃ; tat te pradāsyāmy api ced adeyam
english: Janamejaya said: "O immeasurable one, fitting your youth and handsome form, I grant you a boon as is proper. Choose whatever rests in your heart as desired — I shall bestow it on you even if it be ungrantable."

sanskrit: sūta uvāca patiṣyamāṇe nāgendre takṣake jātavedasi idam antaram ity evaṃ tadāstīko 'bhyacodayat
english: The Sūta said: As the lord of serpents Takṣaka was on the verge of falling into the fire, seizing this interval, Āstīka then urged his request, saying: "This is the moment."

sanskrit: varaṃ dadāsi cen mahyaṃ vṛṇomi janamejaya satraṃ te viramatv etan na pateyur ihoragāḥ
english: "If you grant me a boon, O Janamejaya, this is my choice: let this sacrifice of yours cease, and let no more serpents fall here."

sanskrit: evam uktas tato rājā brahman pārikṣitas tadā nātihṛṣṭamanā vākyam āstīkam idam abravīt
english: The Sūta said: Thus addressed, the king, son of Parīkṣit, O Brahmin, was then not altogether of a rejoicing mind, and spoke these words to Āstīka:
